stances.claim: The Feb. 6 Malacañang induction of new ALA Philippine Chapter officers -- led by CJ Gesmundo as chair -- represents a 'changing of guards' that could have happened in Kuala Lumpur in October 2023, but Gesmundo requested CJ Panganiban to carry on through year-end to allow more time for the SC's 'Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations, 2022-2027.'

Malaysian CJ Tengku Maimun's election as ALA regional president is significant because she is 'the first woman to head the Malaysian judiciary, ALA Malaysia, and the regional ALA' -- a historic triple-first.

PM Anwar Ibrahim's keynote assurance that he 'would protect the independence of the judiciary' is 'refreshing reassurance' in a parliamentary system where parliament is paramount and the judiciary is normally an inferior branch -- particularly because CJ Maimun was appointed by Anwar's defeated predecessor.

In contrast to parliamentary systems like Malaysia's, the PH SC under the tripartite system is the constitutional equal of the President and Congress -- and is often regarded as 'the Most Powerful Court in the World' because of the unique grave-abuse-of-discretion duty.

The 2018 Vietnamese-proposed ALA resolution supporting the Arbitral Award was withdrawn with CJ Panganiban's tacit agreement as ALA Philippines head -- because most other ASEAN delegations were lukewarm given their close commercial, diplomatic, and aid ties with China, and pressing the resolution would have meant 'a sure defeat.'

The recent Marcos visit to Vietnam fortifies the common interest of both countries in upholding the AA and strengthening Unclos advocacy -- and several other ASEAN countries (notably Indonesia) have since 2018 'valiantly asserted their own claims against China's 10-dash line.'

Nonetheless, CJ believes 'regretfully' that ALA -- or even ASEAN itself -- will NOT find any consensus in dealing with China and the South China Sea, given the divergent interests across the ten member states.

notable_anecdotes: CJ Gesmundo's request that CJ Panganiban continue as ALA PH chair past the Kuala Lumpur transition -- preserving institutional continuity while Gesmundo focused on the SC's 'Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations, 2022-2027.'

Triple-first for Malaysian CJ Tengku Maimun: first woman to head Malaysian judiciary, ALA Malaysia, and regional ALA -- making her election a historically significant moment in ASEAN legal institutions.
PM Anwar's whisper to CJ Panganiban during a short private chat as he greeted each delegation head: 'he has many Filipino friends' -- personal-diplomatic detail anchoring the political message.

PM Anwar's assurance of judicial independence in a parliamentary system where parliament is 'the paramount repository of sovereignty' -- and where the judiciary is normally 'viewed as an inferior branch of government' -- drew 'thunderous applause' precisely because of that constitutional baseline.
PH 'Most Powerful Court in the World' framing -- sourced from the unique grave-abuse-of-discretion duty that no other Constitution gives its high court.

Roll-call of ALA Philippines founders (June 25, 1981 SEC certification): senator Edgardo J. Angara as first chair, plus the lineup including future CJs Felix Makasiar and Marcelo Fernan, J Antonio Barredo, Estelito Mendoza, CJ Roberto Concepcion, and others -- historical-foundational documentary device.
Living original members named: Mendoza, Avelino V. Cruz (now ALI chair), Teresita Cruz-Sison, Alonzo Ancheta, and CJ Panganiban himself.
Singapore CJ Sundaresh Menon -- close personal friend of CJ -- turned over the ALA presidency to CJ Maimun in Kuala Lumpur.

2018 Vietnamese-proposed AA resolution: aggressive push, other ASEAN delegations lukewarm, Vietnamese 'sensing a defeat' withdrew the proposal 'with my tacit agreement as ALA Philippines head' -- CJ's most candid insider disclosure about ASEAN diplomatic dynamics on China.
Closing regretful-realism: CJ does not expect ALA -- or even ASEAN -- to find consensus on China/SCS.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban marks a 'changing of guards at Asean Law' on Feb. 6, when President Marcos will induct in Malacañang the new officers of the Asean Law Association (ALA) Philippine Chapter led by CJ Alexander G. Gesmundo as chair -- a handover that could have happened in Kuala Lumpur at the 14th ALA General Assembly (Oct. 17-22, 2023) had Gesmundo not requested CJ Panganiban to carry on as ALA Philippines chair through year-end to give him more time for the SC's 'Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations, 2022-2027.' In Kuala Lumpur, Malaysian CJ Tengku Maimun binti Tuan Mat was unanimously elected ALA regional president for three years -- significant because she is 'the first woman to head the Malaysian judiciary, ALA Malaysia, and the regional ALA.' Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim's keynote emphasizing the rule of law and assuring continued judicial independence drew 'thunderous applause' because, in parliamentary systems like Malaysia's, parliament is the paramount repository of sovereignty and the judiciary is normally 'viewed as an inferior branch of government' -- and because CJ Maimun was appointed by the previous PM whom Anwar defeated. In contrast, in the PH tripartite system the SC is the constitutional equal of the President and Congress, and is 'often regarded as the Most Powerful Court in the World' because of the unique grave-abuse-of-discretion duty. PM Anwar whispered to CJ during a private chat that 'he has many Filipino friends.' The ALA General Assembly accepted the PH offer to host the next Governing Council meeting later this year at New Clark City, where the SC will concurrently host the Conference of Asean Chief Justices (CACJ). CJ lists the new ALA Philippines officers (Regina Geraldez as vice chair; Judge Ralph Jerome Salvador as secretary; Christine Monderin as assistant secretary; J Marian Ivy Reyes-Fajardo as treasurer; Ela Sangalang as assistant treasurer; Ricardo C. Bernabe Jr. as deputy secretary general; Maria Teresa Sison-Go as membership chair; CJ Panganiban as chairman emeritus) and traces ALA Philippines back to its June 25, 1981 founding by Edgardo J. Angara as first chair, J Antonio Barredo, future CJ Felix Makasiar, Estelito Mendoza, J Manuel Lazaro, CJ Roberto Concepcion, future J Flerida Ruth Romero, J Felix Antonio, and future CJ Marcelo Fernan -- with living original members including Mendoza, Avelino V. Cruz (now ALI chair), Teresita Cruz-Sison, Alonzo Ancheta, and CJ himself. Singapore CJ Sundaresh Menon -- a close friend -- turned over the ALA presidency to CJ Maimun in Kuala Lumpur. CJ closes with a candid 2018 disclosure: a Vietnamese-proposed resolution supporting the Arbitral Award in the South China Sea was withdrawn with his 'tacit agreement as ALA Philippines head' after most other ASEAN delegations were lukewarm, given their close commercial, diplomatic, and aid relations with China; the recent Marcos visit to Vietnam fortifies the common AA/Unclos interest, and several ASEAN countries (notably Indonesia) have since 'valiantly asserted their own claims against China's 10-dash line' -- but CJ believes 'regretfully' that neither ALA nor ASEAN will find consensus in dealing with China and the South China Sea.
